summary: Added tests/test_fefx.py, the adversarial and regression suite for the accepted A1 FEFx audit core (tools/measure/fefx.py). The module is loaded by importlib spec into sys.modules exactly as tests/test_measure.py loads tools/measure/premium.py. Eleven tests pin: the gain_matrix valuation convention (district_extrema G equals channel.gain_matrix; TOP/BOT are per-zip max/min), the contract section 13 C0 toys (a) and (b) where EF1 passes on the remove-max residual while FEFx fails on the remove-min residual, the Q0 zero-valued-ZIP divergence (masked FEFx passes on a zero minimum, gain_matrix FEFx fails on a strictly positive one; the valuation field is explicit and n_zero_valued_bundle_pairs separates the conventions), the td/model.py::fairness anchor on a square and a rectangular roster with a genuine EF1 failure (masked valuation, quantifier ef1, slack 1e-12, total-roster divisor n=|R|, legacy keys ef1/n_ef1_failures/envy_over_umax/prop_shortfall all matching to 1e-12), the PairVerdict reason enum with each non-applicable reason counted separately (self=2, empty_bundle=2, empty_own_bundle=3, unmatched_rep=3, infeasible_for_agent=1, applicable=1 over 12 pairs), separate band-only and band-plus-book-overlap feasibility masks (each single-mask call leaves the other off-diagonal pair applicable, ruling out an internal AND), non-finite M and bad parameter rejection, and the empty-retained-roster branch (n=0, all pairs unmatched_rep, prop_gap_min NaN, no ZeroDivisionError). The file deliberately does not import pytest: the frozen .venv has no pytest, and the repository runner (tests/run_all.py) imports every test_*.py directly, so a pytest import would break discovery. raises/close helpers stand in for pytest.raises/pytest.approx.

followups: The cited acceptance command cannot be satisfied until pytest is installed in an environment holding numpy/networkx/scipy; the frozen .venv is intentionally closed. If a pytest run is required for the ledger, either provision a separate test env or record the repository runner as the accepted substitute.

The rectangular fullness check in test_fairness_anchor_rectangular asserts n_unmatched==0: 'unmatched' in the audit counts not-applicable rows (an unmatched envier), whereas rep C is unmatched as an envied-column absence; the fairness anchor itself is the load-bearing equality, the counters are annotations.

Band-only and band-plus-book-overlap masks are caller-built and exercised; once R1/M1 wire the real band mask and S_i(A_j)>0 overlap mask, an integration test should feed those exact masks rather than the synthetic ones here.
learned: The venv ships no pytest, so the repository runner is the only executable acceptance path; writing the file as plain asserts with a local raises/close keeps it runnable under run_all.py and still pytest-compatible if pytest is ever added.

constructing the C0 toys through the real gain_matrix valuation needs only per-zip M with T=free=0 (u_i(z)=lam*M_z), which makes the toy utilities exactly the section 13 numbers and keeps the fixtures synthetic and deterministic.

The masked anchor reproduces model.fairness exactly when |R| >= |D| (every district staffed); a genuine EF1 failure needs a multi-zip envied district and a candidate envier with small own book and large cross book, since a single-zip envied bundle gives v-top=0 and never fails.
Q0's divergence is sharpest when the envier is a non-candidate on the envied district: masked zeroes those zips (BOT=0, FEFx passes), gain_matrix prices the ambient common term (BOT>0, FEFx fails).
